title: A proline-rich Kazal-type serine protease inhibitor is essential for survival and oocyte development in the brown planthopper, Nilaparvata lugens.
abstract: Kazal-type serine protease inhibitors (KaSPIs) play crucial roles in insect growth, development, digestion, metabolism and immune defense. In this study, we identified a specific proline-rich KaSPI in the brown planthopper Nilaparvata lugens. No homologs were found in other organisms. The KaSPI is highly expressed in adult females and is most abundant in the ovaries. RNA interference (RNAi)-mediated knockdown of the KaSPI gene significantly increased mortality in both the nymphal and adult stages and caused severe ovarian malformations, leading to failure of oocyte maturation and oviposition. Furthermore, KaSPI was shown to interact with vitellogenin (Vg) by in vitro and in vivo assays. KaSPI and Vg exhibited similar developmental expression patterns in adult females. Knockdown of KaSPI led to a significant reduction in Vg mRNA and protein levels in ovarian tissues. These findings indicate that KaSPI is not only essential for survival but also critical for oocyte maturation. This study provides new insights into the functional relationship between KaSPI and Vg in N. lugens.

title: Cartilage-hair hypoplasia: A ribosomopathy.
abstract: Cartilage-hair hypoplasia (CHH) is caused by biallelic variants in RMRP, encoding the RNA component of a ribonucleoprotein complex called RNase MRP. Clinically, CHH is characterized by the combination of metaphyseal skeletal dysplasia and T-cell impairment that can lead to a combined immunodeficiency. The spectrum of recognized features includes anemia, autoimmune manifestations and gastrointestinal complications such as Hirschsprung disease. Patients with CHH also have a highly increased risk of developing malignancy, particularly non-Hodgkin lymphoma and basal cell carcinoma. The mechanism linking RNase MRP dysfunction with disease has been debated. Recent studies have clarified that disease-associated RMRP mutations impair pre-ribosomal RNA processing and cause a reduction in mature cytosolic ribosomes, establishing CHH as a ribosomopathy. CHH is also associated with cell cycle defects and shorter telomeres, but whether these features are secondary to the ribosome synthesis defect or driven by other mechanisms remains to be clarified. In this review, we summarize the clinical manifestations and current management of CHH, with a particular emphasis on its hematological and immunological manifestations. We then discuss the evidence linking RMRP mutations to defective ribosome synthesis and appraise possible alternative or complementary disease mechanisms. We also review recently described disorders caused by mutations in protein-coding components of the RNase MRP complex (POP1 and RMP64/NEPRO). Finally, we discuss unresolved questions, including why impaired ribosome synthesis in CHH causes a predominantly T-cell phenotype, in contrast to the erythroid and myeloid failures characteristic of other ribosomopathies such as Diamond-Blackfan anemia.

title: Oncogenic Role of PLOD3 in Melanoma Progression via Wnt/β-catenin Signaling and Tumor Microenvironment Reprogramming.
abstract: Melanoma is an aggressive malignancy, and treatment strategies remain limited for patients with advanced disease, highlighting the need for a better understanding of the driving mechanisms. This study aimed to identify genes associated with melanoma tumorigenesis, characterize their potential mechanisms, and explore the therapeutic relevance and druggability of selected candidates through experimental and computational approaches. Melanoma-related hub genes were screened by integrating weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) with least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression analysis. The biological functions of the candidate gene were validated using proliferation and migration assays in melanoma cells. RNA sequencing was applied to investigate the underlying molecular mechanism, whereas CIBERSORT and xCell analyses were used to investigate the relationship between PLOD3 and immune infiltration. Structure-based virtual screening was performed to explore candidate PLOD3-binding compounds. PLOD3, C4orf48, BUB1, and CD300LF were identified as a melanoma-related gene signature, among which PLOD3 exhibited the strongest association with melanoma progression and metastasis. PLOD3 was significantly upregulated in melanoma and positively correlated with epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) signatures across multiple independent cohorts. Loss-of-function experiments revealed reduced proliferation, migration, and invasion of melanoma cells following PLOD3 depletion. PLOD3 expression was also associated with Wnt/β-catenin pathway activity, and treatment with a pharmacological Wnt/β-catenin activator partially restored the cellular phenotypes suppressed by PLOD3 silencing. Furthermore, elevated PLOD3 expression was associated with reduced CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Structure-based virtual screening identified four candidate compounds-Rosamultin, Actein, Temsirolimus, and Punicalagin-with strong predicted binding affinity to the catalytic glycosyltransferase (GT) domain of PLOD3, supporting its target potential. PLOD3 functions as a critical driver of melanoma progression by promoting Wnt/β-catenin signaling and shaping an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. These findings identify PLOD3 as a promising therapeutic target and provide candidate compounds for further investigation in melanoma-targeted therapy.

title: Tongfengning ameliorates hyperuricemia via inhibiting gut microbiota dysbiosis-mediated TLR4/MAPK/NF-κB hyperactivation in intestinal epithelium.
abstract: To elucidate the phytochemical basis and therapeutic mechanisms of Tongfengning (TFN), a traditional herbal formula used to treat hyperuricemia (HUA), by integrating multi-omics strategies and functional validation. Ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS) was employed to identify the compounds in TFN. A HUA mouse model was induced using hypoxanthine (300 mg/kg) and potassium oxonate (250 mg/kg), followed by oral treatment with TFN at doses of 9.56, 19.11, 38.22 g/kg. Therapeutic efficacy was assessed via serum uric acid (UA) levels, renal function, intestinal barrier markers, and inflammatory mediators. Concurrently, 16S rRNA sequencing was utilized to analyze gut microbiota dynamics, and in vitro co-culture experiments demonstrated that TFN-modulated microbiota protect intestinal epithelial cells (IECs). Mechanistically, network pharmacology and RNA sequencing identified critical signaling pathways, which were subsequently validated by Western blotting. Multivariate statistical approaches were systematically applied to establish relationships between microbiota and HUA biomarkers. TFN significantly reduced serum UA, adenosine deaminase (ADA), xanthine oxidase (XOD) levels (P < 0.01, 0.001), mitigated renal injury, and inhibited pro-inflammatory cytokines (P < 0.05, 0.01, 0.001). TFN reduced serum levels of diamine oxidase (DAO) and D-lactate (D-LA) (P < 0.001), enhanced intestinal mucosal integrity, upregulated UA transporters, and enhanced intestinal UA excretion (P < 0.05, 0.01, 0.001). TFN also restored the Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes (F/B) and mitigated microbiota dysbiosis. In vitro, co-culturing TFN-modulated gut microbiota with IECs directly protected against HUA-induced damage. Integrated network pharmacology with in vivo/in vitro transcriptomics identified the Toll-like receptor 4/mitogen-activated protein kinase/nuclear factor-κB (TLR4/MAPK/NF-κB) axis as the key mechanism through which TFN exerts its therapeutic effects on HUA. Additionally, TFN decreased the abundance of Rhodobacteraceae, Halieaceae, Desulfocapsaceae, Anaerolineae, Akkermansia, Ilumatobacter, and Clostridium, while increasing that of Ruminococcus, Rikenellaceae, Prevotellaceae, Alistipes, Odoribacter, Erysipelotrichaceae, Eubacterium, Muribaculaceae, Monoglobus, Harryflintia, and Muribaculum, which were highly correlated with HUA markers or TLR4/MAPK/NF-κB pathway. This study delineates a mechanistic network connecting the anti-HUA effects of TFN to intestinal barrier restoration, UA excretion, gut microbiota modulation, and TLR4/MAPK/NF-κB pathway inhibition, while identifying key microbial signatures as potential therapeutic targets for HUA.

title: Overexpression of centromere-localized IFIT3 impairs mitochondrial function and disrupts cellular proliferation and cell cycle progression in down syndrome.
abstract: Down syndrome (DS, trisomy 21) is the most prevalent human autosomal aneuploidy, driven by non-disjunction of chromosome 21 during maternal gametogenesis. Centromere-kinetochore complexes mediate accurate chromosome segregation, and centromeric protein dysregulation is linked to chromosome instability; nevertheless, how perturbations of centromere-proximal proteins drive cellular pathogenesis in DS remain poorly defined. We applied CENPA-GFP-APEX2 proximity labeling coupled with LC-MS/MS quantitative proteomics to systematically profile CENPA-proximal proteins in euploid normal amniocytes (NACs) and trisomy 21 DS-derived amniocytes (DSACs). Differentially abundant candidate proteins (DAPs) were biochemically validated by Western blot, followed by bioinformatic enrichment analyses. The top upregulated candidate Interferon-induced protein with tetratricopeptide repeats 3 (IFIT3) was overexpressed in human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) to dissect its functional impacts on DS-relevant cellular phenotypes. RNA-seq transcriptome profiling was conducted to uncover signaling and metabolic pathways perturbed by IFIT3 overexpression, and mitochondrial functional assays were performed to validate bioinformatic predictions. We quantified 999 total CENPA-proximal proteins via label-free proteomics, identifying 32 DAPs in DSACs relative to NACs (19 upregulated, 13 downregulated). Enrichment analyses revealed robust dysregulation of interferon response and ribosomal protein networks in DSACs, with IFIT3 exhibiting the most significant upregulation. Lentiviral IFIT3-OE in pluripotent hiPSCs triggered G1-phase cell cycle arrest, suppressed cell proliferation, and elevated apoptotic rates. Transcriptome-wide RNA-seq demonstrated strong transcriptional repression of oxidative phosphorylation and mitochondrial ATP biogenesis gene sets, accompanied by direct functional deficits including reduced mitochondrial membrane potential and lowered intracellular ATP levels. This study identifies IFIT3 as a highly dysregulated CENPA-proximal candidate protein in fetal DS amniocytes. Gain-of-function assays in hiPSCs confirm that elevated IFIT3 expression is sufficient to disrupt mitochondrial homeostasis and recapitulate core DS cellular defects. Our work provides a novel proteomic framework linking centromere-proximal signaling to mitochondrial dysfunction in trisomy 21, and highlights IFIT3 as a candidate mediator of DS pathogenesis.

title: PIH1D2 Loss-of-Function Directs Ciliary and Cell Cycle Defects Resulting in Left Isomerism With or Without Biliary Atresia.
abstract: Laterality disorders are rare congenital conditions caused by disruption of left-right embryonic patterning, often associated with ciliary dysfunction. Despite the identification of numerous causative genes, the molecular basis remains unresolved in many patients. We aimed to identify the genetic cause of left isomerism heterotaxy in two unrelated patients, and investigate the functional consequences of the implicated gene. Genome sequencing was performed in both patients. Candidate variants were validated by RNA and protein analyses in patient-derived fibroblasts. To study the functional consequences, we conducted RNA-seq, cell cycle assays (flow cytometry, EdU incorporation, Ki-67 staining), rescue experiments with the wild-type gene, and primary ciliogenesis studies. Both patients harboured biallelic loss-of-function variants in PIH1D2, a gene not previously associated with human disease. Transcript analyses confirmed aberrant splicing, and immunofluorescence staining revealed loss of PIH1D2 expression in Patient 1's primary fibroblasts. RNA-seq demonstrated dysregulation of pathways related to cell cycle regulation and developmental signalling. Patient fibroblasts showed impaired cell cycle re-entry from G0 following serum starvation and reduced S-phase progression. Wild type PIH1D2 overexpression partially rescued these defects. Furthermore, patient cells exhibited significantly reduced primary ciliogenesis compared to controls. Our findings establish PIH1D2 as a novel disease gene for left isomerism heterotaxy, with biliary atresia observed in one of the patients. Loss of PIH1D2 impairs ciliogenesis and cell cycle progression, providing a mechanistic link between ciliary defects and abnormal left-right patterning. These results expand the spectrum of cilia-related laterality disorders and identify PIH1D2 as a critical regulator of human development.

title: Transcriptional Profiling Links LNC_501 to Cucumber Responses to Fusarium Wilt and Reveals Fatty-Acid-Metabolism Changes in Host and Pathogen.
abstract: Fusarium wilt is a devastating soil-borne disease that severely limits cucumber production. However, the roles of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in cucumber resistance and the transcriptional interplay between cucumber roots and Foc during infection remain poorly understood. Here, we employed dual RNA-seq to simultaneously profile cucumber mRNAs, lncRNAs, and Foc transcripts in the roots of resistant and susceptible cucumber lines during the early stages of infection. Comparative transcriptome analysis revealed extensive transcriptional reprogramming in both host and pathogen and highlighted cell wall-related and fatty acid metabolism-related processes among the major responses associated with the cucumber-Foc interaction. Functional analyses in transgenic cucumber lines further supported LNC_501 as a putative negative regulator associated with resistance to Fusarium wilt. LNC_501 expression was inversely associated with that of a nearby glycine-rich cell wall structural protein gene, CsGRP1.8, and altered LNC_501 expression in transgenic plants was accompanied by opposite changes in CsGRP1.8 transcript abundance, suggesting a possible role for lncRNA-associated cell wall regulation in cucumber defense. In addition, fatty acid metabolism-related genes in both cucumber and Foc exhibited dynamic and host genotype-dependent expression patterns during infection, suggesting that fatty acid metabolism may be an important shared component of the cucumber-Foc interaction. Together, these findings identify LNC_501 as a candidate lncRNA associated with cucumber responses to Fusarium wilt and suggest a possible link between LNC_501, CsGRP1.8, and cell wall-related defense. They also highlight coordinated fatty acid metabolism changes in both cucumber and Foc during infection, providing a framework for future mechanistic studies of host-pathogen interaction.

title: Lipid-sensing GPR183-KRAS signaling mediates TH17 autoimmunity and identifies fluvoxamine repurposing in uveitis.
abstract: Autoimmune uveitis (AU) is a leading cause of irreversible blindness driven by pathogenic T helper 17 (TH17) cell-mediated inflammation, yet current therapies are limited by efficacy and side effects, with immunometabolic mechanisms remaining poorly defined. By integrating single-cell RNA sequencing and multilayered metabolomic profiling in patients with AU and experimental AU models, we identified the lipid-sensing G protein-coupled receptor GPR183 as a key immunometabolic regulator in pathogenic CD4+ T cells. Upon activation, GPR183 modulates intracellular signaling via suppression of cyclic adenosine monophosphate-cAMP-dependent protein kinase activity and promotion of son-of-sevenless-dependent KRAS activation, which in turn elicits copper overload-induced mitochondrial oxidative stress, structural impairment, and metabolic rewiring toward glycolysis, thereby promoting TH17 cell pathogenicity. For clinical translation, virtual screening of Food and Drug Administration-approved drugs coupled with molecular docking and microscale thermophoresis validation identified fluvoxamine (FLV) as a direct GPR183 antagonist. In in vivo and in vitro uveitis and colitis models, FLV attenuated GPR183-KRAS signaling, dampened pathogenic TH17 cell responses, and alleviated tissue inflammation. These findings delineate a unique GPR183-KRAS-mitochondrial damage axis governing TH17-driven autoimmunity and support repurposing FLV as a translatable therapeutic approach for AU and other autoimmune inflammatory disorders.

title: Targeting Engrailed-1 Fibroblasts in Idiopathic Subglottic Stenosis.
abstract: Idiopathic subglottic stenosis (iSGS) is characterized by pathologic deposition of extracellular matrix (ECM) secondary to dysregulated fibroblasts. Engrailed-1 expressing fibroblasts have been shown to promote ECM deposition in fibrosis. Verteporfin has been shown to reduce EN1 expression in fibroblasts through YAP/TAZ signaling. However, EN1 expression, YAP/TAZ signaling, and verteporfin treatment have not been investigated in iSGS pathogenesis. Biopsies of diseased subglottis and distal healthy trachea of iSGS patients (n = 6) were assessed. qRT-PCR, analysis of iSGS single-cell RNA sequencing data, flow cytometry and immunochemistry were used to compare the expression of EN1. Fibroblasts from diseased iSGS tissue were treated with verteporfin (5 μM) or control and gene and protein expression analysis was performed for EN1, YAP/TAZ pathway and fibrotic genes. The iSGS subglottis demonstrated increased expression of EN1 (fold change = 58.86, SD = 65.12, p: 0.031) compared to controls. Immunohistochemistry analysis of the diseased iSGS subglottis showed that EN1 was densely expressed. Verteporfin treatment of iSGS fibroblasts in vitro led to an 81.75% (SD = 9.28, p: 0.031) reduction in COL1A1 and 22.77% (SD = 17.11, p: 0.031) reduction in COL3A1 gene expression. This was associated with a 26.32% (SD = 28.25, p: 0.031) reduction in EN1 expression and reductions in the YAP/TAZ associated genes AMOTL2, CCN1, CCN2, YAP1, and WWTR1. EN1 and the associated YAP/TAZ signaling pathway are increased in iSGS. Verteporfin treatment inhibited YAP/TAZ expression and attenuated EN1 and COL1A1 expression in vitro. Targeting EN1 expressing fibroblasts through inhibition of YAP/TAZ signaling represents a potential therapeutic target to reduce fibrosis in iSGS. N/A.

title: Vickeline NambaBisfenol A, bisfenol F e DEHP remodel the transcriptome of a human 3D placenta model.
abstract: Microplastics are recognized as important vectors of endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs), including bisphenol A (BPA), bisphenol F (BPF), and di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP). Their recent detection in human placentas has raised substantial concern. However, the precise molecular mechanisms by which these compounds disrupt the placental barrier remain incompletely understood. To investigate the effects of microplastic-associated EDCs on the transcriptome of a human 3D placental model. A human 3D placental model composed of JEG-3 trophoblast spheroids was exposed for 24 h to low concentrations of BPA (1 nM), BPF (1 nM), or DEHP (4 μM). Global transcriptome sequencing was performed using the Illumina NextSeq 2000 platform (paired-end, 2 × 100 bp). Transcript quantification and differential expression analyses were performed using Salmon and DESeq2 (|log2FoldChange| ≥ 1 and FDR < 0.05), respectively. We conducted functional enrichment analysis using clusterProfiler. Oxidative stress markers, including malondialdehyde (MDA) and protein carbonylation, were assessed biochemically. BPA altered the expression of 117 differentially expressed genes (DEGs; 87 upregulated and 30 downregulated), BPF altered 16 DEGs (6 upregulated and 10 downregulated), and DEHP altered 497 DEGs (353 upregulated and 144 downregulated). Both BPA and DEHP increased HSPA1B expression, a key mediator of the proteotoxic stress response, whereas BPF and DEHP downregulated EHMT2, which encodes G9a, a histone methyltransferase involved in chromatin compaction. GO enrichment analysis revealed alterations in processes related to nuclear speckles, RNA splicing, cell adhesion, and syncytialization. Biochemically, descriptive measurements showed higher protein carbonylation levels in BPA- and DEHP-exposed spheroids compared with the vehicle-treated condition. Even at low concentrations, BPA, BPF, and DEHP alter the transcriptome of a human 3D placental model, affecting genes and pathways related to proteostasis, RNA processing, and epigenetic regulation. These findings reveal potential molecular mechanisms of placental toxicity associated with exposure to endocrine-disrupting chemicals, with possible implications in the context of the Developmental Origins of Health and Disease (DOHaD).

title: scTGCL: A Transformer-Based Graph Contrastive Learning Approach for Efficiently Clustering Single-Cell RNA-seq Data
abstract: Motivation: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables characterization of cellular heterogeneity at unprecedented resolution. However, accurate clustering of scRNA-seq data remains challenging due to high dimensionality, dropout-induced sparsity, and technical noise. Existing contrastive learning methods usually create augmented views by perturbing gene expression values, so the uncertainty in cell-cell relationships caused by dropout events is not properly modeled. Results: We propose scTGCL, a novel Transformer-based graph contrastive learning framework that learns robust and discriminative cell representations directly from gene expression data. scTGCL employs multi-head self-attention to adaptively construct weighted cell-cell graphs and a Transformer encoder to generate cell embeddings from them, capturing diverse biological relationships. For contrastive augmentation, we apply feature-level gene masking together with attention masking that randomly drops edges of the learned attention matrices, enabling the model to withstand dropout events and technical noise. A symmetric contrastive loss maximizes agreement between original and augmented representations, while joint optimization with reconstruction and imputation losses preserves biological interpretability. Extensive experiments on twenty real and simulated scRNA-seq datasets demonstrate that scTGCL achieves the highest average performance among nine state-of-the-art baseline methods in clustering accuracy, normalized mutual information, and adjusted Rand index, while also achieving superior imputation performance and substantially lower runtime on large-scale datasets. Furthermore, biological analysis confirms that the learned clusters align with known cell types and yield biologically interpretable pathway enrichment, validating the utility of scTGCL for downstream cell annotation and marker gene discovery. Availability and Implementation: The source code and test data are freely available at GitHub (https://github.com/ShoaibAbdullahKhan/scTGCL)

title: Optimisation of single-nuclei isolation and RNA sequencing of parasitic nematodes
abstract: Single-cell/nuclei transcriptomics has revolutionised our understanding of cell, tissue, and organismal biology in humans and model organisms across health and disease. However, for non-model species, reassessment and refinement of conventional methods is needed to address novel technical and biological challenges. Here, we evaluate three established nuclei isolation protocols and, building on these experiences, develop an optimised protocol for single-nuclei isolation of parasitic nematodes (SNIP). SNIP recovered 1.7- to 4.1-fold more nuclei than the three established protocols, and 3.2-fold more RNA per nucleus than the best-performing of these. We validated SNIP across macroscopic and microscopic life stages and both sexes of two phylogenetically distinct gastrointestinal nematodes, Haemonchus contortus and Trichuris muris, and used it to generate single-nuclei RNA-seq data revealing sex- and stage-specific gene expression and putative tissue-specific expression in both species. By enabling flexibility with frozen samples and consistent recovery across diverse parasitic nematode life stages, SNIP provides a practical foundation for building cell and nuclei atlases in other non-model species, toward advancing understanding from fundamental biology to infection and disease.

title: Keratinocyte-derived CHI3L2 reprograms phospholipid metabolism to promote skin inflammation in psoriasis.
abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disorder characterized by hyperproliferative keratinocytes and a dysregulated cytokine milieu, perpetuating a self-reinforcing inflammatory cycle. Despite the key involvement of keratinocytes in this pathogenic loop, the molecular pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify chitinase-like protein CHI3L2 as a key mediator. Elevated CHI3L2 levels were detected in serum and lesional skin from patients with psoriasis, predominantly in keratinocytes, as also verified by single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomic analyses. In vitro stimulation of keratinocytes with M5 cytokine cocktail (IL-17A, IL-22, oncostatin M, IL-1α, and TNF-α) increased CHI3L2 expression, demonstrating that CHI3L2 is inducible under inflammatory conditions. Transgenic mice expressing human CHI3L2 exhibited aggravated psoriasis-like phenotypes in both imiquimod- and mannan-induced psoriasis models, characterized by epidermal hyperplasia and scaling. To dissect the role of CHI3L2, we used recombinant protein injection, parabiosis, and bone marrow transplantation, identifying keratinocytes as the primary source of pathogenic CHI3L2. This was further confirmed by keratinocyte-specific CHI3L2 knockin mice. CHI3L2 functions in the HaCaT cell line and primary keratinocytes were investigated by recombinant CHI3L2 administration or CHI3L2 knockout. CHI3L2 disrupted phospholipid homeostasis, leading to altered inflammatory responses, proliferation, and differentiation of keratinocytes. CHI3L2 activated secretory phospholipase A2, elevating lysophosphatidylcholine, thereby establishing an autocrine loop perpetuating keratinocyte inflammation and reshaping the immune microenvironment. Therapeutic neutralization of CHI3L2 with antibodies or intervention of phospholipid pathway ameliorated skin inflammation in mouse psoriasis models. Our findings reveal CHI3L2 as an important regulator of keratinocyte-driven lipid remodeling and inflammation in psoriasis, highlighting potential as a therapeutic target.

title: Epigenomic Characterization of Fibroblasts in Darier Disease Identifies Cross-cell-type Regulatory Gene Signatures.
abstract: Darier disease is a monogenic acantholytic derma-tosis caused by mutations in ATP2A2 that primarily disrupt keratinocyte calcium homeostasis. Whether dermal fibroblasts harborharbour disease-associated epigenetic alterations remainremains uncharacterized. In this study, we performed genome-wide DNA methy-lation profiling on primary fibroblasts from lesional and non-lesional skin, followed by STRING protein-protein interaction network analysis to identify regulatory hub genes. Hub gene expression was validated by qPCR and cross-referenced with single-cell RNA-seq data from healthy skin and published RNA-seq data from Darier disease keratinocytes. Lesional fibroblasts showed consistent, site-specific hyper- and hypomethylation converging on inter-connected regulatory hubs. Hypomethylated hub genes included transcription factors and signalingsignalling integrators while hypermethylated hub genes comprised growth-regulatory and adhesion-related genes. Methylation direction predicted transcriptional output at 10 of 12 hub genes by qPCR. These hub genes are expressed across both fibroblast and keratinocyte populations in healthy skin, and lesional keratinocyte RNA-seq data showed directionally concordant expression changes, indicating shared transcriptional dysregulation across compartments. These findings suggest that Darier disease involves a stable fibroblast epigenetic state with cross-cell-type transcriptional relevance, potentially contributing to dermal-epidermal regulatory disruption in lesional skin.

title: Lactate-Induced PPP1R1B Upregulation Drives Resistance to Neoadjuvant Immunotherapy in NSCLC via IRF3 Dephosphorylation.
abstract: Neoadjuvant immunotherapy has improved clinical outcomes in resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); however, a substantial proportion of patients fail to achieve durable responses, and the mechanisms underlying therapeutic resistance remain incompletely understood. Here, we identified protein phosphatase 1 regulatory inhibitor subunit 1B (PPP1R1B) as a metabolic driver of immunotherapy resistance in NSCLC through RNA sequencing of tumors with differential responses to neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 therapy. PPP1R1B was significantly upregulated in non-responders and correlated with poor prognosis in NSCLC patients. Mechanistically, PPP1R1B directly interacted with IRF3 through the Arg29 residue and promoted dephosphorylation of IRF3 at Ser396, thereby suppressing IRF3 activation and downstream interferon-β (IFN-β) signaling. PPP1R1B-mediated inhibition of IFN-β signaling reduced CD8+ T-cell infiltration and impaired antitumor immunity, ultimately conferring resistance to anti-PD-1 therapy in vivo. Blockade of IFN-β signaling abrogated the antitumor effects induced by PPP1R1B depletion, supporting an immune-dependent mechanism. Notably, tumors resistant to neoadjuvant immunotherapy exhibited impaired oxidative phosphorylation and excessive lactate accumulation. Lactate induced PPP1R1B expression through NF-κB-dependent transcriptional activation, linking metabolic reprogramming to innate immune suppression. Collectively, our findings identify a lactate/NF-κB/PPP1R1B/IRF3 signaling axis that drives immune evasion and resistance to neoadjuvant immunotherapy in NSCLC, and nominate PPP1R1B as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for overcoming anti-PD-1 resistance.

title: HnRNPF extensively regulates expression and alternative splicing of genes associated with proliferation and migration in gastric cancer cells.
abstract: Heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein F (hnRNPF) is an RNA-binding protein involved in alternative splicing (AS) regulation and tumorigenesis; however, its role in gastric cancer (GC) remains poorly understood. In the present study, the expression pattern of hnRNPF in stomach adenocarcinoma samples was investigated and hnRNPF knockdown using small interfering RNA in AGS cells was performed. Subsequently, a whole-transcriptome sequencing method, namely RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) was conducted to investigate how hnRNPF regulates gene expression and AS GC cells. Reverse transcription-quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) was performed to validate the molecular targets of hnRNPF. Results indicated that the hnRNPF expression level was significantly increased in tumor samples and associated with nodal metastasis status in patients with GC based on The Cancer Genome Analysis and was also correlated with the overall survival time of patients with GC. RNA-seq analysis identified 929 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and 2,669 hnRNPF-regulated AS events. Functional enrichment analysis revealed that hnRNPF-regulated DEGs were primarily enriched in pathways associated with 'inflammatory response', 'extracellular matrix organization' and 'immune response', which are notably associated with GC progression. In addition, hnRNPF depletion significantly reduced the expression levels of CD55, connective tissue growth factor, frizzled-5, keratin 80 (KRT80) and transglutaminase 2. Furthermore, hnRNPF significantly altered the splicing patterns of key GC-associated genes, including KRT80, CDC25B, CD151, docking protein 1 and ADAM metallopeptidase domain 15. These AS alternations were validated by RT-qPCR and were found to be closely associated with the prognosis result of patients with GC. Collectively, the present findings demonstrated that hnRNPF orchestrates the GC cell transcriptome at both transcriptional and post-transcriptional levels, making hnRNPF a potential candidate for further pre-clinical target evaluation in GC.

title: TREM-1 deficiency attenuates RIPK3/MLKL-associated epithelial injury in Klebsiella pneumoniae-induced acute lung injury.
abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae (KP)-induced acute lung injury involves excessive myeloid inflammation, epithelial barrier disruption, and inflammatory cell death. Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 1 (TREM-1) amplifies innate immune responses, whereas receptor-interacting protein kinase 3 (RIPK3)/mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein (MLKL) signaling contributes to membrane injury. Their relationship during bacterial lung infection remains incompletely understood. KP-induced acute lung injury was established in wild-type and Trem1-deficient mice, and GSK872 was administered prophylactically to inhibit RIPK3. Lung histopathology, inflammatory mediators, and RIPK3/MLKL activation were assessed. Two human lung single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets containing non-fibrotic and fibrotic tissues were analyzed as cross-disease, hypothesis-generating reference cohorts. In vitro, conditioned medium from KP-stimulated THP-1-derived macrophage-like cells was applied to BEAS-2B epithelial cells; macrophage TREM-1 was blocked with LP17, and epithelial RIPK3 was silenced using siRNA. KP challenge increased pulmonary TREM-1 abundance and was accompanied by histopathological injury and altered inflammatory mediator concentrations. Trem1 deficiency reduced these responses together with RIPK3 and MLKL phosphorylation. Prophylactic GSK872 administration produced changes in the same direction. In the human fibrosis reference cohorts, TREM1 was concentrated in inflammatory myeloid populations, and ligand-receptor inference identified candidate macrophage-to-epithelial communication pathways. In vitro, KP increased TREM-1 and inflammatory mediator release from macrophage-like cells. Their conditioned medium induced epithelial membrane injury, RIPK3/MLKL phosphorylation, and loss of E-cadherin and ZO-1; these effects were attenuated by macrophage LP17 pretreatment or epithelial RIPK3 knockdown. Trem1 deficiency attenuated KP-induced acute lung injury and was associated with reduced pulmonary inflammation and RIPK3/MLKL activation. The combined findings support a functional relationship between macrophage TREM-1-dependent inflammatory activation and epithelial RIPK3/MLKL-associated injury, rather than a fully established linear signaling axis. This intercellular injury network warrants further mechanistic and post-infection therapeutic evaluation.

title: Elucidating the toxicogenomic mechanisms of DBP exposure on Hepatocellular carcinoma through network toxicology and molecular docking analysis.
abstract: This study explored the molecular mechanisms by which dibutyl phthalate (DBP) contributes to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) pathogenesis using integrated network toxicology and bioinformatics. DBP's carcinogenic potential was evaluated with ADMETLAB 3.0 and ProTox3. DBP-related targets were obtained from ChEMBL, SwissTargetPrediction, and PharmMapper; HCC-related targets from GeneCards and OMIM. Overlapping genes were identified by Venn analysis. A protein-protein interaction (PPI) network was constructed using STRING and analyzed with Cytoscape to identify hub genes. Functional enrichment analysis (GO/KEGG) was performed with DAVID. Expression validation and survival analysis used TCGA-LIHC and GEO (GSE39791) data. A prognostic nomogram integrating gene expression and clinical variables was developed. Single-cell RNA sequencing (GSE299340) was analyzed with Seurat to examine hub gene expression. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations investigated DBP interactions with core targets. A total of 242 overlapping genes between DBP-associated and HCC-associated targets were identified. PPI network analysis revealed seven hub genes: KRAS, GRB2, ESR1, HSP90AA1, SRC, EGFR, and TP53. Enrichment analysis indicated significant involvement in cancer-related pathways. Expression analysis in TCGA and GEO datasets confirmed significant dysregulation of GRB2, ESR1, HSP90AA1, and SRC in HCC tissues, which correlated with patient survival outcomes. The prognostic model incorporating these genes showed good predictive accuracy. Single-cell analysis indicated distinct expression patterns of ESR1 (hepatocytes) and HSP90AA1 (immune cells) in HCC. Molecular docking demonstrated stable binding of DBP to ESR1 and HSP90AA1 with favorable binding energies (-6.8 and -6.1 kcal/mol, respectively). Molecular dynamics simulations supported the stability of these complexes, with van der Waals interactions being the primary binding force. This integrative analysis suggests that DBP exposure may contribute to HCC pathogenesis by modulating core genes and pathways, although these findings are associative and require experimental confirmation. Hub genes, especially ESR1 and HSP90AA1, are potential biomarkers and targets. Direct DBP-protein interactions provide mechanistic insights into HCC etiology.

title: CNIH4 as a prognostic biomarker and promoter of malignant progression in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is a molecularly heterogeneous malignancy with variable clinical outcomes. Although cornichon family AMPA receptor auxiliary protein 4 (CNIH4) has been implicated in several disease processes, its clinical and biological relevance in HNSCC remains incompletely defined. Transcriptomic, genomic, and clinical data from The Cancer Genome Atlas and independent Gene Expression Omnibus cohorts were integrated for bioinformatic analyses. CNIH4 expression was evaluated in relation to diagnostic performance, clinicopathological features, survival, somatic mutations, tumor mutation burden, immune infiltration, immune-regulatory genes, and drug-response profiles. A prognostic nomogram incorporating CNIH4 was also assessed. Functional studies were performed in SAS and SCC-9 oral squamous cell carcinoma cells using two independent CNIH4-targeting siRNAs. Proliferation, colony formation, and wound closure were measured, followed by RNA sequencing and pathway analyses after CNIH4 knockdown. CNIH4 was consistently overexpressed in HNSCC and validated in three independent cohorts, with retrospective discrimination between tumor and normal tissues in the TCGA-HNSC transcriptomic dataset (AUC = 0.915). Higher CNIH4 expression was associated with unfavorable clinicopathological features and shorter overall survival, disease-specific survival, disease-free interval, and progression-free interval. The nomogram showed moderate prognostic performance, with AUCs of 0.710, 0.750, and 0.720 at 1, 3, and 5 years, respectively. CNIH4 expression was also associated with distinct mutation patterns, higher tumor mutation burden, and differences in bulk transcriptome-derived immune and stromal signatures and immune-regulatory gene expression. Higher CNIH4 expression correlated with lower predicted IC50 values for fluorouracil, tegafur, paclitaxel, and nilotinib. Experimentally, CNIH4 depletion reduced proliferation, colony formation, and wound closure in both cell lines. RNA sequencing revealed changes involving epithelial-mesenchymal transition, interferon signaling, TNF-α/NF-κB signaling, NOTCH signaling, p53-related programs, and the unfolded protein response. This study suggests that CNIH4 is associated with HNSCC progression-related phenotypes and clinical outcomes. Functional and transcriptomic findings support a functional association between CNIH4 and malignant phenotypes in oral squamous cell carcinoma and justify further investigation of its prognostic and therapeutic relevance in HNSCC.

title: High Ubiquitin-like Protein 3 Expression Is Associated With Prolonged Recurrence-free Survival in Non-muscle-invasive Bladder Cancer.
abstract: Current clinicopathological factors inadequately capture the biological heterogeneity of non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC). This study investigated the prognostic significance of ubiquitin-like protein 3 (UBL3), a molecule involved in extracellular vesicle sorting and immune regulation, in NMIBC. Following an exploratory analysis of public RNA-sequencing databases, we evaluated tissue samples from patients who underwent transurethral resection for primary NMIBC. A discovery cohort (n=37) was assessed for UBL3 mRNA via qRT-PCR and protein expression via immunohistochemistry (IHC) quantified using digital H-scores (QuPath). A separate internal validation cohort (n=192) was subsequently evaluated by IHC. The primary endpoint was recurrence-free survival (RFS). The database analysis indicated that high UBL3 expression was associated with longer RFS in early-stage bladder cancer. In the discovery cohort, higher UBL3 mRNA levels were associated with prolonged RFS [hazard ratio (HR)=0.33, p=0.004]. mRNA levels also were associated with digital H-scores (ρ=0.39, p=0.018). In the separate internal validation cohort, elevated UBL3 protein expression was associated with a reduced risk of recurrence. A multivariable Cox regression confirmed that a higher UBL3 H-score (HR=0.95 per 10-point increase, p=0.023), alongside a negative preoperative urine cytology and immediate intravesical chemotherapy, remained independently associated with RFS. Elevated UBL3 expression was associated with prolonged RFS in patients with NMIBC following transurethral resection of bladder tumor. While UBL3 has potential as a prognostic biomarker, establishing its definitive clinical utility will require mechanistic investigations and validation across independent, multicenter cohorts.

title: Donor-aware multi-cohort single-cell analysis identifies an LXR-linked tubular cholesterol-handling state in membranous nephropathy with a coordinated five-gene lipid-remodeling signature across renal tumors.
abstract: Membranous nephropathy (MN) is an immune-mediated glomerular disease in which sustained proteinuria exposes renal tubular epithelial cells to an abnormal filtered-protein load. The tubular metabolic response to this exposure remains incompletely characterized. We investigated whether MN is associated with a reproducible tubular cholesterol-handling transcriptional state and assessed its relationship to protein overload in vitro. We further evaluated whether an experimentally anchored five-gene subset showed a coordinated tumor-associated transcriptional shift across major renal cancer histologies. Three kidney single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets and one glomerular bulk-transcriptomic cohort were analyzed using the donor as the biological replicate. GSE241302 was used for complete-case exploratory discovery, OEP004186 for formal donor-aware support, GSE171458 for directional support, and GSE200828 for tissue-level disease context. A frozen 47-gene LXR-linked cholesterol-handling program and its nested 37-gene cholesterol transport/efflux component were evaluated by donor-level pseudobulk analysis, leave-one-donor-out and leave-one-gene-out sensitivity analyses. HK-2 cells were exposed to protein overload, followed by quantitative reverse-transcription PCR for representative transport and lipid-remodeling genes. The same experimentally anchored five-gene panel was then evaluated in 129 paired tumor-adjacent-normal samples across TCGA-KIRC, TCGA-KIRP, and TCGA-KICH to define a renal tumor-associated lipid-remodeling context. Across all 3 MN donors in GSE241302, program scores were higher than the internal reference in proximal tubule (PT) and loop-of-Henle/thick ascending limb (loop/TAL) compartments. In OEP004186, the program was increased in PT (effect +0.480, false-discovery rate [FDR] 0.0128), PT-VCAM1 (+0.348, FDR 0.0165), and loop/distal epithelial cells (+0.310, FDR 0.0242), with positive effects in every leave-one-MN-donor-out analysis. GSE171458 provided concordant directional support in PT and loop/TAL. The PT-VCAM1 fraction was not increased in MN, whereas the program remained higher within both PT and PT-VCAM1, favoring a within-state transcriptional change. Sixteen program genes showed positive average effects across the three single-cell resources. In GSE200828, the overall program was higher in MN than in living donors (+0.226, FDR 0.0349) but not higher than in other glomerular diseases. Protein overload increased ABCA1, ABCG1, SREBF1, FASN, and SCD expression in HK-2 cells. Across the three renal cancer histologies, the five-gene panel showed a concordant paired increase (REML-pooled effect +0.967, 95% CI 0.843-1.092), and 85.3% of patients exhibited simultaneous increases in the cholesterol-efflux and lipid-synthesis/remodeling arms. MN is associated with a donor-supported LXR-linked cholesterol-handling transcriptional state concentrated in PT and loop/TAL-related epithelial compartments. The state is responsive to protein overload in HK-2 cells and may reflect a broader tubular lipid-homeostasis response to proteinuric kidney injury. The data do not establish direct LXR activation, increased cholesterol-efflux flux, or MN specificity. The paired renal cancer analysis further identifies a coordinated tumor-associated five-gene lipid-remodeling signature across KIRC, KIRP, and KICH, while not establishing tumor-cell-intrinsic LXR activation, immune effects, or a causal tumor mechanism.

title: Integrated Single-Cell Transcriptomics, Multi-Omics, and Mendelian Randomization Reveal Ferroptosis-Related Molecular Subtypes and a Genetically Supported Causal Candidate in Psoriasis.
abstract: Ferroptosis contributes to inflammatory skin diseases, but its role in psoriasis remains incompletely understood. We performed an integrated multi‑omics analysis combining single‑cell transcriptomics, bulk transcriptomics, machine learning, consensus clustering, and Mendelian randomization (MR) to characterize ferroptosis‑related molecular features, intercellular communication, immune microenvironment remodeling, molecular subtypes, and causal biomarkers in psoriasis. Single‑cell RNA‑seq data (GSE151177) were analyzed to quantify ferroptosis activity across cell populations and infer intercellular communication networks. Bulk transcriptomic datasets (GSE30999, GSE78097) were integrated for differential expression and machine‑learning feature selection with SHAP interpretation. Consensus clustering, immune infiltration, functional enrichment, and drug repurposing analyses were performed. Cis‑eQTLs from eQTLGen (n=31,684) served as instruments for two‑sample MR with psoriasis GWAS from FinnGen (13,667 cases, 395,092 controls). Macrophages/monocytes and fibroblasts showed the highest ferroptosis scores. MIF signaling (MIF-CD74/CD44, MIF-CD74/CXCR4, MIF-ACKR3) dominated keratinocyte outgoing communication. Transcriptomic integration yielded 72 overlapping ferroptosis-related genes; machine learning identified eight feature genes (CD24, EFNB2, DDX39A, NDRG4, GPRC5A, S100A8, PRSS8, ITPKC). CD24 (AUC=0.979) and S100A8 (AUC=0.974) exhibited top diagnostic performance. Consensus clustering stratified patients into two subtypes (C1, C2); all eight genes were highly expressed in C1, while C2 showed upregulated phagocytic but downregulated innate immune pathways. Drug enrichment suggested MS-275, genistein, and β-adrenoceptor agonists as potential ferroptosis-modulating compounds. MR demonstrated that only PRSS8 eQTL had a nominally significant causal association with psoriasis risk (P < 0.05, β = 0.0073). Our multi‑omics study delineates the ferroptosis‑related landscape in psoriasis, identifies MIF signaling as a key keratinocyte communication axis, establishes a high‑performance diagnostic model with eight feature genes, defines two distinct immune‑metabolic subtypes, and provides genetic evidence supporting PRSS8 as a putative causal biomarker for psoriasis susceptibility, offering novel insights and potential ferroptosis‑based biomarkers and therapeutic targets for psoriasis.

title: Prediction of therapeutic targets and drug candidates for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma by network-based computational framework.
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the most lethal malignancies, with limited therapeutic options and an urgent need for novel treatment strategies. This study presented a network-based computational framework for in silico genome-wide therapeutic target identification and drug discovery. A network-based computational framework was developed that integrates transcriptomic data from multiple independent PDAC cohorts to construct gene co-expression networks. Prognostic gene signatures were incorporated to identify feature modules via hypergeometric enrichment analysis. Key regulatory genes within these modules were prioritized using multi-metric centrality analysis. Functional relevance of candidate targets was assessed using single-cell ribonucleic acid (RNA) sequencing, genome-wide clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) dependency datasets, and clinical survival analyses. To enable therapeutic translation, this study implemented a transcriptome-guided drug discovery strategy to systematically match pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC)-specific gene expression signatures with compound-induced transcriptional profiles from the Library of Integrated Network-based Cellular Signatures (LINCS) database. Candidate compounds were ranked using a cross-cohort consensus scoring approach and subsequently evaluated in vitro using quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR), Western blotting, and cell viability assays. Comprehensive analysis of multi-cohort PDAC transcriptomic data identified 14 key genes with high network centrality, including three potential oncogenic drivers: Cytoskeleton associated protein 2 like (CKAP2L), kinesin family member 18A (KIF18A), and minichromosome maintenance 10 replication initiation factor (MCM10), which exhibited tumor-specific overexpression and poor prognostic associations. Single-cell RNA sequencing (ScRNA-seq) revealed their predominant expression in epithelial tumor cells, while CRISPR screening confirmed functional essentiality. The transcriptome-guided drug discovery approach matched these targets with LINCS perturbation profiles, identifying mitoxantrone/OTSSP167 (CKAP2L inhibitors), PF-3758309 (KIF18A inhibitors), and vorinostat (MCM10 inhibitors) as candidate therapeutics. Experimental validation using qRT-PCR, Western blotting, and cell counting kit-8 (CCK-8) assays collectively demonstrated the dose-dependent therapeutic effects of these compounds, showing significant mRNA suppression, corresponding decreases in protein levels, and potent anti-proliferative activity in PDAC cells. This study establishes a robust, network-based framework for therapeutic target discovery and transcriptome-driven drug prediction in PDAC. It identifies three novel, functionally essential oncogenic drivers and proposes clinically actionable compounds, offering a scalable approach for addressing undruggable targets in cancer therapy.

title: Integrated transcriptomic and single-cell analyses define neuronal heterogeneity and PDIA4-associated malignancy in glioblastoma.
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is characterized by extensive cellular heterogeneity and complex interactions between malignant cells and the surrounding microenvironment. The contribution of neuronal populations to GBM progression and prognosis, however, remains incompletely understood. Bulk transcriptomic data from TCGA-GBM and GTEx were integrated with two single-cell RNA-seq datasets. Differential expression analysis, WGCNA, machine-learning-based survival modeling, CIBERSORT, GSEA, CopyKAT, MiloR, pseudotime analysis, GSVA, CellChat, and pySCENIC were used to characterize prognostic genes and their cellular context. PDIA4 was further examined in U251 and U87 cells using siRNA-mediated knockdown followed by Western blotting, qPCR, Transwell invasion, wound-healing, colony-formation, and CCK-8 assays. Nine prognostic genes-PDIA4, CAMK2N1, RPH3A, RAB11FIP4, DMTN, EPHB6, SLC47A2, ESM1, and EMILIN2-were retained in the final prognostic model. Single-cell analysis showed distinct cellular distributions of these genes and identified a tumor-associated neuronal population enriched in GBM. Pseudotime analysis revealed transcriptional differences between normal- and tumor-associated neuronal states, while CellChat predicted altered NRXN-NLGN communication involving neuronal populations and GBM cells. Immune deconvolution showed associations between several prognostic genes and immune-cell composition, including an inverse correlation between PDIA4 and activated NK cells. Experimentally, PDIA4 was expressed at higher levels in U251 and U87 cells than in SVG p12 cells. PDIA4 knockdown reduced clonogenic growth, invasion, wound closure, and CCK-8 metabolic activity readouts in both GBM cell lines. Integrative bulk and single-cell analyses linked GBM prognosis to distinct neuronal and immune features of the tumor microenvironment. Together, these analyses place the nine-gene prognostic signature within the cellular architecture of GBM and highlight tumor-associated neuronal states as a potential component of the prognostic tumor ecosystem. PDIA4 knockdown provided complementary functional support for one component of the signature, while the predicted NRXN-NLGN network nominates a candidate route of neuron-GBM communication for future investigation.
